renewable-nonrenewable-s1.title: An island chooses its energy
renewable-nonrenewable-s1.html:
Our island burns imported diesel for almost all of its electricity. Every liter arrives by ship, so when storms close the harbor or prices jump, the whole island feels it. Some neighbors say we should burn wood from our hills instead, but our forest is small and its trees take decades to regrow; burning it for power would not be renewable in practice. We should instead build on what arrives here for free every day: the steady trade wind and strong sunshine. Batteries can carry us through the evening, and a small diesel supply can stay as a backup for the rare calm, cloudy week. Each year of local power is a year of fuel we do not have to buy.
